title: ZDX API rate limits: the license tiers, the headers, and how the clients pace themselves

prose.text: ZDX limits requests per tenant tier, and each client paces itself in its own way. The server side is documented once for all OneAPI products.

prose.label: The server's limits.
prose.text: The tier table is [[shared.oneapi.rate-limits:zdx-tiers]], the windows start with the first call ([[shared.oneapi.rate-limits:window-starts-first-call]]), and rate-limited clients must back off exponentially ([[shared.oneapi.rate-limits:back-off-exponentially]]). {{graphql-tiers}} Whether the two tables number the same tiers is open {{gap:tier-numbering}}; the GraphQL limits are also in [[shared.analytics.graphql-errors-and-limits:zdx-graphql-limits]].

prose.label: Headers.
prose.text: The documented headers are [[shared.oneapi.rate-limits:zdx-headers]]. The SDKs' direct clients read differently named per-second headers {{divergence:header-names}}, and which family each host sends is open {{gap:header-family-per-host}}.

prose.label: How the clients pace.
prose.text: The Go OneAPI client's ZDX limiter is [[shared.oneapi.rate-limits:go-zdx-limiter-copies-zcc]]. The Go direct client's fixed limiter paces only its sign-in ([[zdx.sdk-go.legacy-client:limiter-auth-only]]) and its backoff waits a fixed time chosen from the per-second headers and the status code ([[zdx.sdk-go.legacy-client:backoff]]). The Python executor's wait on a 429 comes from `Retry-After` or the reset header ([[shared.sdk-python.retries:wait-from-headers]]), and its legacy ZDX client reads the per-second headers only around sign-in ([[zdx.sdk-python.legacy-client:second-headers]]). {{no-tier-awareness}} The earlier question about reconciling the client limiters with the tier is closed by this reading {{gap:tier-vs-client-limiter}}.

checks.do: Which tier the tenant's license count puts it in, and which window (second, minute, hour or day) a 429 came from.
Which header a hand-written client reads for its remaining budget, and whether that header is present on the host it calls.

graphql-tiers.statement: The ZDX GraphQL API's rate limits are based on the license tier level and have five tiers: tier 3 is 40,000 licenses at 5 per second, 120 per minute, 6,000 per hour and 30,000 per day, tier 4 is 100,000 at 12, 300, 15,000 and 75,000, and tier 5 is more than 100,000 at 12, 450, 22,500 and 150,000. The ZDX API's own table has four tiers, with 100,000 licenses at tier 3 and more than 100,000 at tier 4 ([[shared.oneapi.rate-limits:zdx-tiers]]).

quotes: Rate limits for the ZDX GraphQL API are based on the license tier level.
every endpoint is called from a specific IP address and the rate limit is dependent on the Tier Level.

graphql-tiers.conditions: Absence: `python3 -I scripts/help_capture.py text vendor/zscaler-help/automate-zscaler/<page>.json | grep -c 40,000` gives 1 for rate-limiting-analytics-zdx-graphql-api-rate-limits and 0 for rate-limiting-zdx, so the 40,000 tier is on the GraphQL page only.

no-tier-awareness.statement: Neither SDK reads the tenant's tier: the Go limiters are fixed constants (100 calls per hour on the OneAPI client, 100 per 60 seconds on the direct client's sign-in) and the other pacing reacts only to what a request gets back: response headers, a 429 or another status, or no response.
no-tier-awareness.conditions: A reading of the limiter and backoff code at the pin; neither SDK has a setting for the license tier.

header-names.summary: The rate-limit header names: the ZDX rate-limiting page documents `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset`; the SDKs' direct clients read `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Second` and `X-Ratelimit-Limit-Second`.

quotes: - x-ratelimit-remaining: The number of API requests remaining for the current rate limit window.

positions.says: The remaining budget is in `x-ratelimit-remaining`, for the current window.
The Go direct client reads the remaining budget from `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Second`.
The Python legacy client reads `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Second` on a sign-in 429.

header-names.impact: If the server sends only the documented headers, the SDKs' proactive per-second backoff never engages and they fall back to their 429 handling; a hand-written client that reads the SDKs' names would see nothing.

tier-numbering.title: Whether the ZDX API and ZDX GraphQL API rate-limit tables number the same license tiers
tier-numbering.detail: Each page scopes its table to its own API. From tier 3 the numbers differ (100,000 licenses is tier 3 on the ZDX API page and tier 4 on the GraphQL page), and neither page says whether a tier number is one scale across both or defined per API.
tier-numbering.blocks: saying which limits a tenant gets on the GraphQL API from its tier on the ZDX API

header-family-per-host.title: Which rate-limit header family each ZDX host sends
header-family-per-host.detail: The rate-limiting page names `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset` without saying which host; the SDKs' direct clients read `X-Ratelimit-*-Second` headers. An earlier note that the gateway sends a `RateLimit-*` family has no source at the pin. Only a captured response from each host would settle which headers arrive where.
header-family-per-host.blocks: writing client-side pacing that reads the right header

tier-vs-client-limiter.title: Whether the SDKs' client limiters are reconciled with the tenant's tier
tier-vs-client-limiter.resolution: They are not: the limiters are fixed constants and the direct Go client's limiter paces only sign-in (claim no-tier-awareness; zdx.sdk-go.legacy-client:limiter-auth-only).
